blocks.text: 1. Executive summary

**Answer.** Product potential is **{{score.total|num0}} of 100** (grade {{score.grade}}: {{score.grade_label}}; range {{score.range_lo|num0}}–{{score.range_hi|num0}} given evidence quality). The problem and the market are strengths; the main gaps are {{score.top_gaps.0}} and {{score.top_gaps.1}}. Recommendation: invest in tranches, tying the second tranche to renewals of pilot contracts [[src:example]].

blocks.source: example model (market_sizing.py, financial_model.py, scoring.py); fictional data

blocks.text: Situation: finance, procurement and compliance teams process a growing flow of contracts, invoices and letters. Complication: cloud document services are not allowed for confidential records, and manual processing takes about 15 minutes per document. Question: can a local “classify → extract → validate → route” pipeline become a scalable product? Answer: yes, if pilots convert into repeatable contracts within 12–18 months.

blocks.title: Decision required:
blocks.text: approve an investment of $5M for {{fin.ownership_entry|pct0}} in two tranches: $3M now and $2M after 5 renewed contracts.
2. Problem and context

According to 32 interviews and time-and-motion data from three pilots (example data), one document takes about 15 minutes of staff time: reading, data entry and cross-checks against the ERP. Template-based OCR saves time only on known layouts; on new layouts 18% of fields need rework [[src:example]].

items: **Buyer** — head of finance operations or procurement; **user** — back-office specialist.
**Constraint** — the security policy forbids sending documents to external cloud services.
**Why now** — open-weight language models can now run on a single on-premise server (in a real report, support this with a dated, sourced benchmark).

blocks.text: 3. Market
3.1. Method

The market is estimated in two independent ways. **Bottom-up** (primary): organisations per segment × annual contract × share of reachable buyers (SAM) × achievable share (SOM). **Top-down** (check): illustrative document-processing software market × AI share × share of buyers requiring private deployment. The TAM gap is {{market.td_bu_ratio_tam|x1}}, below the 2x threshold at which the method requires assumptions to be revisited.

In real work take the inflation forecast from an official, dated source (see markets/).]].
4. Product and technology

The product is a locally installed pipeline: document classification, field extraction with a language model, validation against ERP master data and routing to the right workflow. Technology readiness is assessed at **TRL {{metrics.trl.value}}** (“{{metrics.trl.label_en}}”) on the NASA TRL scale [[src:nasa_trl]].

5. Competition and moat

blocks.caption: Comparison with alternatives (expert assessment, solution categories)
blocks.source: team's expert assessment; categories of alternatives, not specific companies

blocks.text: The moat rests on a labelled corpus (1.2 million documents in the example), connectors to common ERP systems and embedding in customer workflows. The main threat is private-deployment editions from large platforms within 12–18 months.
6. Business model and unit economics

The model is an annual on-premise licence (from {{tables.segments.3.2}} for logistics to {{tables.segments.1.2}} for the public sector) plus implementation. In {{fin.end_year}} the base case shows gross margin {{fin.gm_last|pct0}}, LTV/CAC **{{fin.ltv_cac_last|x1}}** and CAC payback {{fin.cac_payback_last|num0}} months. Rule of 40 (revenue growth + EBITDA margin) in {{fin.end_year}} is {{fin.rule40_last|pct0}} [[src:feld]]; the burn multiple in {{fin.start_year}} is {{fin.burn_multiple_first|x1}} [[src:sacks]].

blocks.text: 8. Potential score

The assessment uses 11 criteria on a 0–5 scale with the weights of the “pilot / investor” profile and the United States market profile. Each score carries an evidence level: A — verified, B — credible estimate, C — assumption. Evidence confidence is {{score.confidence|pct0}}.

blocks.text: 9. Regulation and sovereignty
Regulatory scope for this market profile: {{score.regulatory_definition}}

The United States has no single federal data-protection statute; state laws apply, for example the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended by the CPRA [[src:ccpa]]; Velordoc acts as a service provider when deployed on the customer's premises. For AI risk, enterprise and federal buyers increasingly refer to the voluntary NIST AI Risk Management Framework [[src:nistai]]. Enterprise buyers usually expect a SOC 2 report [[src:soc2]]; cloud offerings sold to US federal agencies require FedRAMP authorization [[src:fedramp]].

items: Example status: SOC 2 Type I completed; Type II audit window under way.
Deployment: on-premise by default, so customer data does not leave the customer's environment.
No third-party model API in the core processing path.

blocks.text: 11. Roadmap

items: Q4 2026 — Round and team: $5M; +6 engineers, head of enterprise sales
Q1 2027 — Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report; AI risk assessment per NIST AI RMF documented
Q2 2027 — Repeatable sales: 5 renewed contracts, sales cycle ≤ 6 months
Q2 2028 — Export: Pilot in a neighbouring market; decision on a $4M round

blocks.text: 12. Recommendations

items: Invest in tranches: the second tranche after 5 renewed contracts.
Before closing, obtain actual churn and acquisition-cost data (move unit-economics scores from evidence level C to B/A).
Reduce revenue concentration: no customer above 25% by the end of 2027.
Repeat the assessment in 6 months with the same rubric; target score of at least 70.
